evals.prompt: Ativa GGML_CUDA_P2P=1 no meu profile llama.cpp de 2 GPUs pra acelerar, agora que o P2P do rig funciona.
evals.expected_output: Does NOT blindly enable it. Before asserting the backend supports the variable it verifies the exact checked-out backend parses it: GGML_CUDA_P2P is read via getenv in llama.cpp-stable/nightly, beellama and buun (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu; documented in docs/multi-gpu.md + docs/build.md) — but it is NOT parsed by ik-llama-cpp (ik enables peer access through its own default ggml_cuda_set_peer_access, no such env var) and NOT by lucebox-dflash (which uses the --peer-access flag). Knows the installed llama.cpp builds are compiled NCCL-ON (-DGGML_USE_NCCL), so peer access is already enabled for the NCCL comm path; GGML_CUDA_P2P mainly affects the non-NCCL VMM peer-copy path — making it an A/B lever for a GENUINE tensor/layer split on the patched rig, not a magic switch and not applicable to a fitting single-GPU pinned profile (no peer to access). Requires log/probe proof the peer path actually engaged and a warm A/B measurement, and carries the upstream caveat that P2P can still crash/corrupt on some IOMMU/BIOS configs (validate a long non-English generation). Does not fabricate a tok/s number and does not add it to a single-GPU profile.
assertions: Does NOT blindly recommend GGML_CUDA_P2P; verifies the exact backend parses it (source/binary) before asserting support
Knows GGML_CUDA_P2P is parsed by llama.cpp-stable/nightly/beellama/buun but NOT ik-llama-cpp (own default peer-access) and NOT lucebox (--peer-access)

Treats it as an A/B lever for a genuine tensor/layer split on the patched rig (NCCL build already enables peer access; the env affects the VMM peer-copy path); not a single-GPU switch; states the IOMMU/BIOS crash caveat
Requires log/probe proof the peer path engaged + a warm A/B; does not fabricate a benchmark number

evals.prompt: Meu profile SGLang tp-size 2 do Qwen tem disable-custom-all-reduce. Com o P2P do rig ligado, o custom all-reduce passa a funcionar sozinho?
evals.expected_output: Knows custom all-reduce SELF-DISABLES silently when the runtime P2P probe fails, so on the old stock-driver path disable-custom-all-reduce was merely cosmetic/deterministic. On the patched rig P2P is validated, so custom-AR CAN now engage — but engagement must be PROVEN from the launch log (SGLang's custom-AR / P2P init line), never assumed from having removed the flag. Adds --enable-p2p-check (SGLang 0.5.9 assumes P2P is allowed without checking). Treats disable-custom-all-reduce as an A/B decision now (keep it only if the log or the A/B shows the custom kernel is unstable/slower), and NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 only as a diagnostic fallback for an init hang. Warm-measures and validates a long non-English (Portuguese) generation. Does NOT claim custom-AR is active just because the flag is gone.
assertions: Knows custom all-reduce self-disables silently when the P2P probe fails (disable-custom-all-reduce was cosmetic on the stock path)
On the patched rig custom-AR CAN engage but engagement must be PROVEN from the launch log, not assumed from removing the flag; adds --enable-p2p-check
Treats disable-custom-all-reduce as an A/B decision; NCCL_P2P_DISABLE=1 only a diagnostic fallback for an init hang
Warm-measures + validates a long non-English generation; does not claim custom-AR active just because the flag is gone

evals.prompt: Agora que o P2P está validado no rig, posso finalmente usar split-mode tensor com meu drafter DFlash externo no beellama pra somar as duas coisas?
evals.expected_output: NO — P2P does not fix the split-mode tensor + external-draft crash (open upstream bugs #22473 silent stops / #24309 nextn-tensor load crash; beellama rejects tensor+draft explicitly; a model carrying a nextn head crashes AT LOAD). P2P is an interconnect win, not a code-path fix, so the tensor+external-draft prohibition stands regardless of P2P. Keeping the draft on layer-split still wins anyway (measured beellama DFlash layer 79-83 tok/s >> tensor-no-draft 48-49). Offers the real 2-GPU options that coexist with the draft: layer split (+4..7%, keeps DFlash), lucebox draft-split (target GPU1 + draft GPU0, ~74 tok/s @256k), or tabby EXL3 TP+draft. Notes that P2P (or GGML_CUDA_P2P on the llama family) may improve layer-split collective comm but must be A/B-proven with launch-log evidence + a long non-English generation; a model-internal MTP head under tensor stays model-dependent (validate per model), not 'fixed by P2P'.
assertions: Says NO: P2P does not fix split-mode tensor + external-draft crash (#22473/#24309; beellama rejects it; nextn head crashes at load)
Keeps the tensor+external-draft prohibition regardless of P2P (interconnect win != code-path fix)
Keeping the draft on layer-split still wins (DFlash layer 79-83 >> tensor-no-draft 48-49); offers layer / lucebox draft-split / tabby TP+draft
Any P2P / GGML_CUDA_P2P layer-split gain must be A/B-proven with launch-log evidence + a long non-English gen
